cross_references.description: CPNI/AT&T liability is the gateway; Wiretap Act §2511 captures the downstream harm. AT&T's CPNI failure enabled the SIM swap; the SIM swap enabled the interception of Michael's communications in transit. AT&T's negligence is the but-for cause of the §2511 violations by McClaran. AT&T may be liable as a facilitator of those violations ($10,000/event + mandatory fees).

AT&T's CPNI failure → SIM swap → stored communications accessed. AT&T's negligence caused the SCA violations by enabling the account takeover that accessed stored emails, voicemails, and account records.

cross_references.short_title: Bus. & Prof. Code §17200 — UCL Unfair Business Practices
cross_references.description: Because 47 U.S.C. §222 has no private right of action, UCL §17200's 'unlawful' prong is the primary California civil remedy path for AT&T's CPNI violations. AT&T's violation of 47 C.F.R. §64.2010 = unlawful business practice; UCL adds injunction + restitution to the negligence damages.

cross_references.short_title: Cal. Penal Code §§630-638 — California Invasion of Privacy Act
cross_references.description: AT&T's CPNI failure → SIM swap → CIPA §632.7 violations (cellular interception). AT&T is the but-for cause of the CIPA violations as the carrier that processed the fraudulent port.
